seo.title: Local SEO Checklist for 2026: 30 Steps for Local Businesses
seo.meta_description: A local SEO checklist for 2026 with 30 practical steps: Business Profile, listings, website, reviews, links, AI search and tracking, from Anaheim.

h1: The Local SEO Checklist: 30 Steps for Anaheim and Orange County Businesses
answer: This local SEO checklist covers 30 steps in six areas: your Google Business Profile, listings, website, reviews, local links and tracking, plus AI search checks. Work through it in order and most Anaheim and Orange County businesses will fix the problems that hold back their local rankings and AI recommendations.
key_takeaways: Then fix listings and your website.

sections.heading: How to use this checklist
sections.body_html: Work through each section in order and mark each step done, not started or not relevant. The early steps fix the foundations; the later ones build reputation and track results. Revisit it every quarter.

sections.heading: Business Profile (steps 1-6)
sections.body_html:
1. Claim and verify your profile.
  2. Use your real-world business name without keywords.
  3. Choose the most accurate primary category.
  4. Add genuine secondary categories and every service.
  5. Set accurate regular and holiday hours.
  6. Add real photos of your premises, team and work.

sections.heading: Address and service area (steps 7-9)
sections.body_html:
1. Use a real address you operate from; Google says virtual offices are not eligible.
  2. If you visit customers, set a service area.
  3. Do not use P.O. boxes.

sections.heading: Listings (steps 10-13)
sections.body_html:
1. Check your name, address and phone on Apple Maps, Bing Places and Yelp.
  2. Fix industry directories.
  3. Remove duplicates.
  4. Keep one phone number per location.

sections.heading: Website (steps 14-20)
sections.body_html:
1. One page per main service.
  2. Direct answers at the top of each page.
  3. Your name, address and phone on every page.
  4. LocalBusiness or a specific structured data type.
  5. Fast, mobile-friendly pages.
  6. Real links between pages so Google can crawl them.
  7. An about page with real people.

sections.heading: Reviews (steps 21-24)
sections.body_html:
1. Create a Google review link or QR code.
  2. Ask every customer.
  3. Reply to reviews.
  4. Never offer incentives.

sections.heading: Local links (steps 25-27)
sections.body_html:
1. List memberships in local and industry groups.
  2. Earn mentions from partners and suppliers.
  3. Support local events or causes you genuinely care about.

sections.heading: AI search and tracking (steps 28-30)
sections.body_html:
1. Ask ChatGPT, Gemini and Google about your services monthly and record results.
  2. Track calls, directions and clicks in your profile.
  3. Watch Search Console and AI referral visits in Analytics.

sections.heading: Why each area matters
sections.body_html: Google's Business Profile help says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and popularity. It explains prominence as how well-known a business is, drawing on how many websites link to it and how many reviews it has, and says more reviews and positive ratings can help. It also says there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking.

sections.heading: Priorities if you are short on time
sections.body_html: If you can only do five things this month: fix the profile category and services, correct your name, address and phone everywhere, create a review link and start asking, build pages for your top two services and set up call tracking.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Skipping verification.
  • Inconsistent phone numbers.
  • Cloned city pages.
  • No review routine.
  • No tracking.

sections.heading: Quarterly review
sections.body_html: Every quarter, re-check hours, categories and photos, scan listings for changes, review rankings and calls and rerun your AI questions.

sections.heading: Details businesses often overlook
sections.body_html:
• Holiday hours.
  • Duplicate profiles created by previous staff or agencies.
  • A website contact page with an old phone number.
  • Structured data that does not match the profile.
  • Robots.txt rules that block important pages.

sections.heading: How to prioritise when everything looks broken
sections.body_html: Fix what customers see first: your profile details, phone number and hours. Then fix what confuses search engines: inconsistent listings and duplicates. Then build what earns new visibility: service pages and reviews. Measuring comes last only because you need the basics in place to measure anything meaningful.

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.body_html:
• NAP: name, address and phone number.
  • Citation: a listing of your NAP on another site.
  • Structured data: code that describes your business to search engines.
  • Crawlable link: a standard link search engines can follow.
  • Search Console: Google's free tool for site search performance.

sections.heading: How long each stage usually takes
sections.body_html: Profile fixes can be done in an afternoon, though verification can take longer. Listing cleanup usually takes a few weeks, because some platforms are slow to process changes. Website improvements depend on how many services you offer; one good service page might take a day to write and check. Reviews and local links build over months. Tracking can be set up in a day and should be in place before you judge whether anything is working.

sections.heading: Keep the checklist alive
sections.body_html: Save the checklist as a shared document, assign each step to a person and note the date it was last checked. A living checklist prevents the slow drift that causes most local SEO problems.

sections.heading: Checklist for a new business
sections.body_html: If you are just opening, prioritise steps 1 to 9 and 14 to 17 before launch: a verified profile, accurate address or service area, a website with clear service pages and your details on every page. Start asking for reviews from your very first customers.

sections.heading: Checklist for an established business
sections.body_html: Established businesses usually have the basics but accumulate problems: old listings from a previous address, outdated hours, duplicate profiles and pages that no longer match services. Steps 10 to 13 and the quarterly review matter most for you.

sections.heading: A worked example: a Huntington Beach roofer
sections.body_html: A Huntington Beach roofer works through the checklist and finds its phone number differs on Yelp and an old directory, its profile lacks tile roof repair as a service and its website has one page for all roofing work. Fixing those three things, then adding pages for tile repair and roof replacement and a review routine, addresses the biggest gaps in a few weeks.

sections.heading: Tools that help
sections.body_html:
• Google Business Profile performance reports.
  • Google Search Console.
  • Google Analytics.
  • A simple spreadsheet of every listing and its details.
  • Call tracking that keeps your main number on listings.

sections.heading: How AI search fits in
sections.body_html: Steps 28 to 30 are the AI part of the checklist. Ask ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google the same questions each month, note who is named and why, and fix the gaps the answers reveal: missing services, wrong details or too few reviews.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Profile, listings, website, reviews, links, tracking. Do them in that order and repeat.

faqs.q: What is a local SEO checklist?
faqs.a: A step-by-step list of the tasks that help a business rank in local search.

faqs.q: What is the first step in local SEO?
faqs.a: Claim, verify and complete your Google Business Profile.

faqs.q: How often should I review local SEO?
faqs.a: Quarterly, plus whenever your details change.
It helps Google read your details; add LocalBusiness or a specific type.
Only when genuinely useful; near-identical pages risk Google's doorway policy.

faqs.q: How do I track local SEO?
faqs.a: Business Profile performance, Search Console, Analytics and your lead records.

faqs.q: Is AI search part of local SEO?
faqs.a: Increasingly; check what AI assistants say about you monthly.

faqs.q: Can I do local SEO myself?
faqs.a: Most of the checklist, yes; technical fixes and content production are where many businesses get help.

faqs.q: Which step has the biggest impact?
faqs.a: For most local businesses, completing the Business Profile and starting a steady review routine.
